title: DiffusionE: Reasoning on Knowledge Graphs via Diffusion-based Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Existing KG reasoning methods struggle as propagation steps involve increasing numbers of entities and can produce semantic inconsistency during message aggregation.

gap.claim: Prior methods neglect interactions between adjacent entities and propagation relations during KG message propagation.

contributions.claim: Introduces DiffusionE, a knowledge graph embedding method based on a diffusion process.
Reformulates message propagation in knowledge reasoning as a diffusion process in which message semantics serve as the diffusion signal.
Provides theoretical analysis suggesting that optimal diffusivity can be leveraged for message propagation in semantic KG interactions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe DiffusionE as a novel knowledge graph embedding method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that semantic information enables effective and adaptive message transmission between nodes.
The authors report that DiffusionE leverages message interactions between entities and propagation relations, ensuring semantic consistency in KG reasoning.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance compared with prior work on several established benchmarks.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs have demonstrated strong capabilities for reasoning over knowledge graphs.
Prior message-propagation paradigms struggle with expanding entity involvement and neglect semantic interactions, causing semantic inconsistency.
DiffusionE addresses these issues by modeling message propagation as a diffusion process driven by message semantics.
Theoretical analysis suggests using optimal diffusivity for semantic interactions in KG propagation.
The authors report semantic consistency and state-of-the-art benchmark performance.

source_observation.claim: Prior propagation methods neglect interactions between entities and relations, which leads to semantic inconsistency.

interpretation.claim: Message-passing designs should model interactions among both participating entities and relation semantics.

application.claim: For relational graph reasoning, evaluate whether aggregation preserves consistency between node messages and propagation relations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this design principle applies beyond the reported KG reasoning setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmarks, metrics, datasets, or numerical performance results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results.
The abstract does not detail the theoretical assumptions or derivation of optimal diffusivity.
